text:
metric-bot: ALERT hosted-api p99 latency spike: 600ms baseline -> ~2.4s, p95 up from 120ms -> ~700ms. Detected across us-west-2 pool.

anya: seeing it on dashboards too. spike started ~1799001180. p50 steady. looks like tail. :thinking_face:

mike: queue depth on the serving runtime jumped. backlog count from 2 -> 18 per instance. Could be batching wait.

shreya: I rolled a small change to batching heuristics yesterday (reduce max wait from 50ms -> 20ms) but that should *lower* latency, not spike it. did that coincide with the rollout? @deploy-bot any deploys?

deploy-bot: deploy: service/hosted-api rollout completed 1799001120 by shreya. canary healthy at completion.

anya: ok canary was healthy but maybe under load different. I'll pull a flame graph from the runtime. give me 60s.

infra-bot: FYI noisy-tenant detection flagged tenant=acme-inc with heavy small-req pattern starting 1799001100. per-tenant reqs/sec ~3x baseline.

mike: small requests -> poor batching packing -> more kernel selection churn. our kernel selector is sensitive to seq_len distribution. if reqs are short and distributed, continuous batching may create many tiny batches with more scheduling overhead.

shreya: can we confirm kernel selection jitter? I can run profiler on a replica.

anya: profiler snippet (top functions, 10s sample):
```
runtime_kernel_select  34%  (increased)
runtime_batch_wait     22%  (vs 3% baseline)
kv_cache_lookup        18%  -> 41% (evictions up)
scheduler_lock         12%  (contention)
others                 14%
```

anya: batch_wait jump looks suspicious. batch wait means the scheduler is delaying to try to gather better batch — but we reduced max wait earlier. might be a logic inversion for tiny requests where we actually wait longer due to packing heuristic.

mike: also seeing kv cache miss rate jump from 2% -> 27% for the same time window. suspect thrash: many tenants generating unique prefixes causing many KV entries and evictions.

simon: putting numbers from `rbctl metrics` (per-instance):
```
instance=hosted-12 backlog=17 batch_size_median=1 batch_size_95=4 kv_evictions_minute=520 kernel_switches=340
```

shreya: wow batch_size_median=1 — so we're not benefiting from batching. That plus high backlog means requests are queued waiting for a kernel slot, then dispatched singly. latency tail due to scheduling and kernel selection overhead per batch.

anya: hypothesis: noisy tenant drives many single-token requests which cause KV cache churn, pushing other tenants' KV entries out -> more cache misses -> kernel paths that are slower (non-quantized fallback) -> per-request overhead skyrockets.

mike: mitigation options: 1) short-term: throttle acme-inc at edge (rate-limit) or move to separate pool; 2) immediate: revert packing heuristic change to previous conservative behavior; 3) medium: increase KV cache size or change eviction policy (LRU -> freq-aware).

shreya: can we try #1 now? infra can add a temporary quota for tenant=acme-inc.

infra-bot: applied soft-rate-limit 60r/s for tenant=acme-inc at 1799001250.

anya: dashboards showing p99 dropping already. new p99 ~840ms and trending down. p95 ~220ms.

mike: nice. we should still root-cause the packing heuristic regression — maybe an off-by-one in the wait timer that made it *longer* for tiny requests. I'll run the unit that changed the wait logic through a local microbenchmark.

shreya: I'll open a PR to revert the change and include a stress test for tiny-req workloads.

simon: logging note: captured a representative trace for a slow request:
```
# trace 1799001219
enqueue -> wait_for_batch (waited 46ms) -> kernel_select (12ms) -> kv_lookup (miss) -> kernel_fallback (quantize path) -> model_exec -> return
end-to-end: 2450ms
```

anya: 46ms wait is wrong given the target max 20ms. that confirms logic regression.

mike: followups: - revert heuristic rollout (shreya) - add packing stress test (mike) - increase kv cache pressure metrics and per-tenant eviction alerts (anya) - consider tenant isolation options for Dedicated pools (product/discussion)

shreya: created PR #1842 to revert and added unit tests. linking: https://git.redwood/pr/1842 :thumbsup:

anya: I'll keep monitoring the next 30m. thanks all. :rocket:

metric-bot: RESOLVED: p99 back to 780ms after infra soft-limit and revert PR queued. incident duration ~8 minutes.

mike: postmortem note: small-request noisy tenants can amplify scheduler heuristics and KV cache behavior -> tail latencies. action item: add synthetic tiny-req workload to continuous perf suite.
